clue.text: Cars that may go with 15?

definitions.meaning: old, battered cars are called ... in British slang
sausages, the partner of mash (15 across) in the British dish of sausages and mash

explanation.surface: A question about which vehicles pair with some other entry.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers and mash is the classic British pub dish of sausages with mashed potato; a banger is also a clapped-out old car.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the same word for a sausage and for a rickety old motor car.

clue.text: Vessels answer with speed, oars flying

parts.note: miles per hour, a measure of speed

indicators.note: the oars fly about wildly, so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Boats respond quickly as the rowers' oars thrash about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats, fitting the oars, but these are ancient storage jars; 'flying' scrambles the oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek two-handled jars are vessels in the sense of containers, not ships.

clue.text: Exchange of lead in film?

parts.note: lead here is bullets, traded back and forth in a western shoot-out, not the starring actor

explanation.surface: Swapping the leading actor during a movie shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' wants to be the star of the film; read as the metal, it is bullets flying both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-out is literally an exchange of bullets, often a set piece in westerns.

clue.text: Condition of one wearing new summer hat?

indicators.note: the hat is worn by the one, so the numeral sits inside the other letters
the summer hat is made new, its letters remade in fresh order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Asking what ails someone sporting a new straw hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SUMMERHAT, and 'wearing' places I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatism is a medical condition causing pain and stiffness in joints and muscles.

clue.text: Trade that's expensive having changed sides

indicators.note: right (R) is swapped for left (L), a change of side

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: A costly business transaction that has switched parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having changed sides' swaps R (right) in DEAR for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: To deal is to trade or do business, as in dealing in antiques.

clue.text: Debacle if backing a second business

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word if is read in reverse

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A disaster looms if you invest in a second firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IF into FI; 'backing' looks like financial support in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A humiliating total failure is both a debacle and a fiasco; the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Detailed reason nervous reaction is bitter in tone

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the word for reason loses its tail letter

parts.note: a cause is a reason
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A thorough account of why a jittery response sounds sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as de-tailed, so CAUSE loses its last letter to give CAUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic remarks are sharply sarcastic and cutting, a bitter tone of voice.

clue.text: Professional impression is ultimately important

parts.note: a dent is an impression pressed into a surface

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word important

explanation.surface: A professional's making an impression really does matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives the final T of 'important'. The definition is the noun: a professional person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist is a qualified professional, an example of one who practises a profession.

clue.text: Consider varying diet adopted by friend

indicators.note: taken in by the friend, so the mixed letters go inside

parts.note: mate is British slang for friend

indicators.note: the diet is varied, so its letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Think about switching to a diet your friend has taken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' means taken in, so the scrambled diet letters go inside the friend; 'mate' is British for friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate on something is to think deeply about or ponder it.

clue.text: Sales talk about a new canine

indicators.note: the patter goes around the other letters

parts.note: a spiel is a glib sales patter

explanation.surface: A salesman's pitch about a new dog for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places A and N inside SPIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog, an example of a canine.

clue.text: Such eyes may find keys regularly in cupboard

definitions.note: an adjective for eyes of a particular kind, the clue saying eyes may be this

indicators.note: the chosen letters go inside the cupboard

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word keys

explanation.surface: Sharp eyes might spot keys left in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'such eyes may be', describing eyes rather than naming them; 'regularly' picks the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes positioned unusually near each other on the face are described as narrowly spaced in this way.

clue.text: Tiger perhaps has a record broadcast — and another record!

parts.note: a tiger is an example of a big cat

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word's sound gives the letters

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Tiger Woods has a record televised, then another record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that LOGUE sounds the same as LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list or register of items, a record of another kind.

clue.text: Platform providing power and widespread dislike

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
odium is general hatred or disapproval

explanation.surface: A stage that brings both influence and unpopularity.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand on which a speaker or winner stands, a small stage.

clue.text: They may offer you protection inside boat after storm

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Shelter below deck when a storm has hit the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges INSIDEBOAT; 'inside' looks like a position word but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins made by the immune system defend the body against infections.

clue.text: Appetiser butcher's cooked, with thanks

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A starter the butcher has prepared, served with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like kitchen work in the surface but is the anagram signal; 'ta' is British informal thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruschetta is Italian toasted bread with toppings, served as a starter.

clue.text: Service ends prematurely with hotel food

indicators.note: the word stops early, losing its last letter

parts.note: Mass is a church service
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Hotel meal service cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends prematurely' cuts MASS to MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is mashed potato, a staple British food, especially with sausages.

clue.text: Pilots suffering with gastroenteritis?

definitions.note: pilot schemes, test versions run before the real thing

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal, a source of suffering
the runs is slang for diarrhoea, a symptom of gastroenteritis

explanation.surface: Airline pilots laid low with a stomach bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilots' looks like aviators; here it is the plural noun for test runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilot schemes are preliminary tests, the same as rehearsals before full launch.

clue.text: Black perhaps, medium and not as smooth

parts.note: the Black Sea is an example of a sea
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
less means to a smaller degree, not as much

explanation.surface: A black garment, medium size, and not quite so silky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' wants to be a colour; here it names the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seamless has no joins, so it is perfectly smooth and continuous.

clue.text: City's dash, for example after victory

definitions.note: the clue's apostrophe s reads as 'city is'

indicators.note: the dash and the example come after the victory

parts.note: a win is a victory
to nip is to dash quickly, as in nip to the shops

explanation.surface: A city's sprinter, say, after winning a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' orders the charade so the victory comes first; 'City's' is 'City is', linking to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is a Canadian city, capital of the province of Manitoba.

clue.text: Couple may see pig turning up in book

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair might spot a pig appearing in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes WOS from SOW; 'in' puts it in TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple and a twosome are both pairs of people together.

clue.text: Handy form of communication?

parts.note: handy literally means using the hands, as in the sign language of deaf people

explanation.surface: A convenient way of keeping in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' wants to mean convenient; read literally it means done with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sign language communicates through hand shapes and gestures.

clue.text: Leave be, with no end of mess

indicators.note: with no means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to exist is to be

indicators.note: the end of mess is its final letter

explanation.surface: Let things be and stop making a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives the S of 'mess', which 'no' removes from EXIST. 'Leave be' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart, as in exiting a building.

clue.text: Image witch improved for spells?

definitions.note: spells collectively, the benevolent sorcery itself

indicators.note: the words are improved, reworked into a better arrangement

explanation.surface: A witch has tidied up her image to cast good spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improved' rearranges IMAGEWITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign sorcery used for good ends, the kind of spells good witches cast.

clue.text: Cut in duty

definitions.meaning: to remove surgically or edit out
a tax levied on goods produced within a country

explanation.surface: A reduction in tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling is a verb meaning remove by cutting and a noun meaning a domestic goods tax.

clue.text: Compassionate, putting crew in shade

indicators.note: the crew goes inside the shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Kindly, sending the staff into the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to staff a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing kindness and mercy toward people or animals.

clue.text: Definite about changing nice and easy position needing little effort

indicators.note: the certain word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: sure means certain, definite

indicators.note: the word nice is changed, its letters moved around

explanation.surface: Definitely switching to a nice cushy job with little to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easy' belongs to the definition, not to the anagram; 'about' wraps the certain word around the changed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work, a cushy job.

clue.text: Salt-free diets must include grass

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: Low-sodium diets need some grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Salt-free diets'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses growing in wetlands.

clue.text: Try a daily worker in case of treatment

indicators.note: the worker goes inside the case
the case of the word is its outside, first and last letters

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, often hired by the day

explanation.surface: Give a day labourer a go at handling some treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' means the outer letters of 'treatment', which hold the worker between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort or try at something.

clue.text: Large church must entertain current senior politician

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, holding the other letter inside

parts.note: a minster is a large church, like York Minster
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cathedral must host a senior member of the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must entertain' places I inside MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister heads a department, a senior political office-holder.

clue.text: Sort of dog food put in front of 15?

definitions.meaning: the meat in the dish ... and mash, coming before mash (15 across)

explanation.surface: A question about a pet and which food precedes another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: Sausage and mash is the British pub dish; a sausage dog is the nickname of the dachshund.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a dog breed nickname and the meat in a classic British dish.
